monument_name: Bistabara Stone Memorial Pillar (erected in 1500 CE)
description_en: Bistabara Stone Memorial Pillar, dated ŚS 1422 (1500 CE), is located five meters north of a complex of threeśikharatemples (JUM0450,JUM0451andJUM0452) beneath the village of Bistabara. The Pillar is a slab with an arched top. The north-eastern side of the Pillar is embellished with a flower or star motif on top and a horse turned to the left below. The lower register of the pillar contains a five-line inscription in Nāgarī script.  The execution of the inscription is crude and has now deteriorated. Nonetheless, the date of installation of the Pillar, ŚS 1422 (i.e., 500 CE), can be read.From the 13th to the 17th centuries, stone pillars were built throughout the Karnali Basin. They are erected to honour the memory of deceased people, most of whom were warriors (Andolfatto 2019). According to P. R. Sharma's interpretation of the inscription, the Pillar was installed by Biju Rāuta and his wife Sāvala Rāuta, and it mentions Viṣṇu's blessings (Sharma 2012: 181). According to Sharma, the flower or star motif on top of the pillar is Viṣṇu's war discus (Skt. cakra).
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number JUM0453_I_001 Sources Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.

historical_events.event_description: As previously stated, the Pillar contains a five-line inscription in Nāgarī script, and the execution of the inscription is crude and now severely eroded. P. R. Sharma published the inscription's content (Sharma 2012: 181). The following is his reading and translation: “Oṁ svasti sāke 1422 biju rāut saptani sā wala rāut ... vishnu subhaṁHail! sake 1422 Biju Rāut with his wife Sāwala Rāut ... Vishnu (does) well for all”.
